caption:
You spent three hours picking interests. Your creative was always doing the targeting.

Meta's delivery has been getting broader and better at the same time for years. Give it a wide audience and a clear creative, and it finds the people who respond. Give it a narrow audience and a vague creative, and it has nothing to work with.

Here's the part that actually matters: whoever your ad speaks to is who answers it. An ad that opens "if you run a clinic and your front desk misses calls" has targeted clinic owners more precisely than any interest list could. The words do the filtering.

So the lever isn't the audience panel. It's the first line.

Write the first line for one person with one specific problem, say who it's not for, and let the system go find them. That's cheaper, faster, and it survives every targeting change Meta ships.

📌 DM me the word AUDIT and I'll send you the 20-minute version, or grab it from the link in my bio.
